([[Putnam, Connecticut]]) | college = [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] (2017–2018) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | highlights = | medal_templates = {{MedalSport | Men's [[basketball]]}} {{MedalCountry|the {{bk|USA}}}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|FIBA Americas U18 Championship]]}} {{MedalGold| [[2016 FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship|2016 Chile]] | [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|National team]]}} {{MedalCompetition|[[FIBA Under-19 World Cup]]}} {{MedalBronze|[[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup|2017 Egypt]]|}} }} '''Hamidou Diallo''' (born July 31, 1998) is an American basketball player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky Wildcats]]. He was a consensus 5-star prospect, and one of the top rated basketball players in the class of 2017. ==High school career== Diallo attended [[John Bowne High School]] in [[Flushing, New York]] during his freshman and sophomore year. As a sophomore, he averaged 17.1 points, 6.6 rebounds per game, and 2.7 assist. During the 2015 summer, Diallo competed on the [[Under Armour]] Association Circuit (UAA) for the AAU team, NY Jayhawks. He averaged 22.5 points and 5.0 rebounds per game on the 2015 Under Armour Association Circuit. Later that summer Diallo was invited to both NBPA Top 100 and [[Adidas]] Nations camps. Diallo transferred to Putnam Science Academy in [[Putnam, Connecticut]] prior to his Junior Year. As a junior, he averaged 17.0 [[Points per game]], and 4.0 rebounds while leading Putnam to a (35-7) overall record. In the 2016 summer, Diallo then joined the AAU team, New York Rens on the Nike Elite Youth Basketball League (EYBL) Circuit. He averaged 18.6 points, and 2.1 assist while leading the Rens to the season-ending Peach Jam. As a senior in 2016-17, he averaged 19.0 points, 6.0 rebounds, and 3.0 assist where he led the Mustangs to a (38-3) record. Diallo was considered one of the top players in the 2017 recruiting class by [[Scout.com]], [[Rivals.com]] and [[ESPN]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.scout.com/college/basketball/recruiting/story/1712117-hamidou-diallo-is-eligible-for-the-nba-draft|title=Hamidou Diallo is eligible for the nba draft, will consider all options|last=Daniels|first=Evan|date=September 29, 2016|work=|access-date=November 5, 2016|via=Scout.com}}{{Cite news|url=http://www.scout.com/player/195220-hamidou-diallo|title=Hamidou Diallo, Putnam science Academy SG - Scout|last=|first=|date=|work=|access-date=January 7, 2017|via=Www.scout.com}}{{Cite news|url=http://n.rivals.com/content/prospects/1734|title=Hamidou Diallo - Rivals.com|last=|first=|date=|work=|access-date=January 7, 2017|via=Www.rivals.com}} Diallo was heavily recruited by six schools, [[University of Kentucky]], [[University of Arizona]], [[Indiana University]], [[University of Kansas]], [[Syracuse University]], and [[University of Connecticut]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/blog/collegebasketballnation/insider/post?id=116462|title=Will five-star Hamidou diallo bypass college for NBA|last=Borzello|first=Jeff|date=November 21, 2016|work=|access-date=November 25, 2016|via=Www.espn.com}} ==College career== On January 7, 2017, Diallo committed to the [[University of Kentucky]].{{Cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/18427587/five-star-wing-hamidou-diallo-commits-Kentucky-Wildcats-enroll-next-week|title=Hamidou Diallo, No. 11 in ESPN 100, picks Kentucky over UConn|last=Borzello|first=Jeff|date=January 7, 2017|work=|access-date=January 7, 2017|via=Www.espn.com}} He would start participating with the team in practices, but would not play a single game that year due to his late entry into the program. Diallo was one of a record-high 182 players to declare for the [[2017 NBA Draft]], despite not having played a single college game in the process. On May 24, 2017, Diallo announced that he would return to Kentucky to play in their 2017-2018 season, despite draft scouts saying he could have been taken in the first round of the draft that year. On November 10, 2017, Diallo scored 18 points, 3 assist, and 5 rebounds to defeat [[Utah Valley University|Utah Valley]]. On November 12th, Diallo recorded 16 points and 3 assist in a 73-69 win against [[University of Vermont|Vermont]]. On November 22nd, he scored 19 points and 3 rebounds to help the Wildcats defeat [[University of Illinois at Chicago]] in the Adolph Rupp Classic. On December 2, 2017, Diallo recorded 19 points, 2 assist, and 2 steals in a 79-70 victory against [[Harvard University|Harvard]]. On December 9th, Diallo scored 23 points and 2 rebounds in a win against [[Monmouth University]] in the Citi Double Cash Classic. On December 16th, he scored 20 points, 3 steals, and 2 assist to defeat [[Virginia Tech Hokies|Virginia Tech]]. ==National team career== Diallo competed for the [[United States men's national under-19 basketball team|under-18 United States national basketball team]] that captured gold in the [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]] game in 2016.{{Cite news|url=http://www.newenglandrecruitingreport.com/news/diallo-wins-gold-with-usa-basketball|title=Diallo wins gold with usa basketball|last=|first=|date=July 24, 2016|work=|access-date=January 7, 2017|via=Www.newenglandrecrutingreport.com}} He won bronze at the [[2017 FIBA Under-19 Basketball World Cup]] in [[Egypt]]. ==References== {{reflist|3}} ==External links== *[http://www.ukathletics.com/sport/m-baskbl/2016/roster/58768df5e4b071b6cedb7648 Kentucky Wildcats bio] *[https://www.usab.com/basketball/players/mens/d/diallo-hamidou.aspx USA Basketball bio] {{DEFAULTSORT:Diallo, Hamidou}} [[Category:1998 births]] [[Category:Living people]] [[Category:American men's basketball players]] [[Category:American people of Guinean descent]] [[Category:Basketball players from New York (state)]] [[Category:Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball players]] [[Category:Shooting guards]] [[Category:Sportspeople from Queens, New York]]
